title: "A multispecialty educational intervention to improve acceptance of organs from donors with HIV: the analysis code"
format: html

## The study

The HOPE Act made it legal in the United States to transplant organs from donors with HIV into recipients with HIV, but such organs were used less than expected, including at the authors' transplant center. In December 2020 the center held a multispecialty educational intervention to address the barriers its transplant teams had identified. Swaminathan and colleagues compared the periods before (March 2018 to November 2020) and after (December 2020 to April 2022) the intervention [@swaminathan2025hope]. The share of declined offers that were declined for potentially HIV-related reasons fell from 93% (25/27) to 63% (49/78). The rate of transplants per patient-year on the waiting list roughly tripled (incidence rate ratio 3.11, 95% CI 1.08 to 9.44), and the rate of transplants from donors with HIV rose more steeply (16.3, 2.90 to 305). The [clinical background](quarto/background.qmd) page says more.

## What this site does

The original analysis was a single R Markdown file (shown [here](quarto/original.qmd)). This repository rebuilds it as scripts that `R/main.R` runs in order, and this site explains each script step by step. The rebuilt code is written to reproduce the published numbers; every place where it differs from the original code, or where the paper differs from the code, is listed on the [differences page](quarto/differences.qmd).

::: callout-note
## Patient privacy
The code is published without the values that could identify patients. The intervention date (day 0 for both study periods), one record-level correction and the random seed used by the patient timeline are kept with the restricted study data, not in the code. With the exact intervention date, the day offsets in the analysis would give each patient's event dates. The correction recodes one accepted offer as a provisional acceptance, because the recipient became ineligible before transplant. The patient timeline moves each event by up to two days, so it is no more precise than the published figure.
:::

## Methods

The authoritative specification is the [analysis plan](quarto/analysis-plan.qmd). In brief: a single-center before-and-after comparison. Offers from donors with HIV to the center's candidates are compared by period, including declines for refusal codes considered potentially HIV-related. Transplant rates are compared with Poisson regression on one record per candidate per day of follow-up. Candidate, donor and transplant characteristics are compared by whether and how candidates were transplanted.

## Status

The code is complete and tested on synthetic data. Run on the study data by the maintainer, it reproduces the published incidence rate ratios and the published counts checked so far. Open decisions are tracked as [GitHub issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/hope-act-education-intervention/issues). The site shows code and methods only; for the results, see the [published article](https://doi.org/10.1111/tid.70039).
